WS presented in two major forms: generalized and localized. Generalized WS was reported in 21 patients (44%) (Figure 1a–c). Localized WS was observed in 27 patients (56%), predominantly affecting acral sites such as the upper and lower limbs in 15 cases (56%). The head and trunk were involved in nine cases (33%), while the trunk alone was affected in three cases (11%).

Other subtypes included papulonodular (12 cases, 25%; Figure 1e–g), vesiculobullous (10 cases, 21%; Figure 2a), granuloma annulare‐like (5 cases, 10%; Figure 2b, c), and cellulitis‐like (3 cases, 6%; Figure 2d).
